chapter: The Sound of Jazz and Lester Young
title: Robert Herridge's improvising camera crews
summary: Herridge picked camera operators who could improvise, and later fell out of favor with young TV executives.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: It was fantastic and the look on her face, you know the way she’s just groovin’ to what he’s playing. And I’m thinking like it must have been a wonderful moment but also sort of anxious, like, are the cameras working? Are we getting that?

Oh Herridge did all kinds of stuff on television. He did Faulkner, he did Conrad Aiken. He had his own free-form thing. And before we did that show he had picked out, he knew, he was at CBS a long time, he picked out cameramen and women who could improvise. He said don’t worry about being in the shot, that doesn’t count. The studio is the studio. There’s no set. And never mind what you hear from the control room. If you get a shot, use it. And that’s why we have some of the shots in there, like Basie listening to Monk and all that stuff. But Herridge finally fell out of favor on commercial television and his last show was on PBS and he tried hard and he said to me, “all these executives are in their twenties and they never heard of Lester Young.”
